title: Priority quorum shedder and rollbackable fallback bridge
author: Aisha Khan
description:
Context: We observed repeated bursts that caused regional egress saturation and global SLO churn. The existing global shedder reacted too coarsely (heavy collateral for low-priority tenants) and the temporary workaround (static egress caps) caused high error rates for critical onboarding flows. This PR introduces two coordinated mechanisms: (1) a Priority Quorum Shedder (PQS) inside the serving runtime that performs minimal cohort shedding based on per-tenant priority quorums and request cohorts; and (2) a Rollbackable Fallback Bridge in the control plane that transparently redirects shed requests to a lower-cost fallback path (fallback model variant or alternate region) while maintaining an easy rollback.

Design summary: PQS maintains lightweight per-tenant priority queues and computes a quorum set of in-flight requests that can be shed to restore the regional latency SLO. The algorithm prefers shedding low-priority cohorts across many tenants rather than all requests from a single tenant. The quorum decision is traffic-aware and respects configured fairness weights. The Fallback Bridge provides a policy layer that maps shed decisions to fallback targets, with safe guards (rate-limited bridge, circuit protection, and per-region egress cap). All new behaviors are gated behind feature flags (pqs.enabled, pqs.bridge.enabled) and a small control-plane rollout window.

Why this is different: Rather than indiscriminate rate-shedding, PQS seeks a minimal, explainable reduction (the quorum) that keeps high-priority work alive. The Rollbackable Bridge is designed to be reversible and observable: enable -> canary -> scale -> roll back without service restarts.

Telemetry & metrics added: pq.shed.count, pq.shed.latency_target, pq.quorum.size, pq.quorum.affected_tenants, pq.bridge.fallback_rate, pq.bridge.rate_limited, pq.rollback.marker. Dashboards and alerts added under Observability > PQS.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy runtime changes to canary nodes with pqs.enabled=false. 2) Enable pqs.enabled=true on 5% of canaries and monitor pq.shed.count and regional egress metrics for 24h. 3) Enable pqs.bridge.enabled=true on canaries, validate fallback success rate < 2% errors. 4) Gradually increase canary percentage and then rollout to mainline. Emergency rollback: flip pqs.enabled=false and pqs.bridge.enabled=false; bridge maintains idempotent rollback markers to avoid stale state.

Safety controls: per-region emergency egress cap (configurable), circuit-breaker on bridge (min success threshold), TTL markers for rolled-over requests, and detailed telemetry to detect regression.

Runbook notes: added docs/runbooks/pqs-runbook.md with step-by-step rollback and SLO thresholds. The runbook includes escalation to SRE and instructions to revert canary traffic via the console and feature flags.

Related work items: ENG-3421 (SLO-driven shedding prototype), ENG-3489 (fallback mapping), SUP-432 (customer incident root cause), and an internal experiment for fairness weighting (ENG-3560).

release_notes:
- Add Priority Quorum Shedder (PQS) to the serving runtime to reduce SLO churn with minimal-cohort shedding.
- Introduce Rollbackable Fallback Bridge to route shed requests to safe fallback targets (feature-gated).
- Per-region emergency egress cap to mitigate egress quench incidents.
- New metrics and dashboards under Observability > PQS.
- Feature flags: pqs.enabled, pqs.bridge.enabled; default off for safe rollout.
